title: Solo-developed a Steam game in 3 months with "vibe coding"—now facing the real boss: marketing
author: hwantasticgames
selftext:
Fingers crossed this doesn't get flagged as spam! I've been building up karma for days just to post here. :)

Blessed by the power of "vibe coding," I've been solo-developing a PC game for about three months now, and I'm currently prepping for its Steam release. As I near the finish line, it’s really hitting me that building the game was only half the battle—marketing is where the real work begins.

The core development was pretty much wrapped up by early August. But since this is my first time launching on Steam solo, I found myself hesitating and fumbling around—wondering how to handle the demo, open playtests, and next steps—and ended up losing about two weeks without making much real progress.

One funny quirk about vibe coding: I hate letting unused tokens go to waste, so I've actually started working on a second game I had only vaguely brainstormed before. It really is a technology that forces you to stay productive!

Anyway, I realized I still need some more time before kicking off full-blown marketing. Today, I just wanted to share a lighthearted post to ease my mind a bit, after spending the last few days feeling anxious about promotion not going as smoothly as I'd hoped.

Here’s the Steam page for the game I'm getting ready to launch:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5015250/Hearts\_Extreme/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5015250/Hearts_Extreme/)  
*(Wishlisting it would be a huge help!)*

I’ll be back soon with more proper devlogs. More than anywhere else, I’d love to share the joys and pains of this journey with my fellow vibe coders here!

comments.author: Water-Cheese
comments.body: One thing I will say is the game's UI screams AI, that may draw unwanted attention.

replies.author: Gurkage
replies.body: That's something I thought too. Just 'looks" vibe coded.

replies.author: account009988
replies.body: Always surprises me they take all this effort to vibe code a whole game but rarely bother to change the default ai slop ui. It is ugly af and a dead give away for slopware

replies.author: ForeignInformants
replies.body: I wish Wikipedia’s entry for vibe coded used this person’s game as image.

comments.author: perrinashcroft
comments.body: This looks like an AI webgame more than a steam game. I think you are going to really struggle with the Steam audience. They're already cautious about AI stuff, but even if you'd hand coded this it doesn't look competitive amongst the card games on Steam. Good work finishing a project and always worth taking it to release but I would be careful how much you invest in marketing, set your expectations fairly reasonably.

comments.author: Count_Triple
comments.body:
I'm a year into my big project but have about 7 other side projects with fully designed frameworks just waiting to be built.   
I too hate wasting credits so I usually design projects while driving to work. I have the ai ask me one question at a time until the vision is solidified. I also use these discussions for criticism push back or set up scenarios to test the design.   
There's only so much time I can actually spend on the computer building/testing so the big project's game loop is top priority.

comments.author: ScutFarkush
comments.body: I would take some time to in ai the visual element. I have been working on a game also and this is where I have spent much more time than I expected, but it really makes a difference in the feel of the game. At this level of solo dev, having charming well thought out art style wins more points than even gameplay sometimes.

comments.author: lexblauvelt
comments.body: Agreed on UIUX. Making the game look like anyone with an agentic subscription can one shot it with the right prompt

comments.author: truongan2101
comments.body: Do you think you get back 100$ with this game?

replies.author: USDJPYFX
replies.body: Not a chance he will lol

comments.author: Open_Organization997
comments.body: Art aside, why would anyone want to play this game ?

comments.author: PerfectSituation1668
comments.body:
Like the other comments said: UI looks AI, so steam users won't like it. The voluntary saying of AI usage is appreciated more than hiding it. Your use of emoji and bullet points in the text screams of AI use. I don't know how the translation works on the backend of steam, but in my version it said "**Laat het ons weten op Discord:**" (Dutch for let us know in the discord) and there was no discord link. It just said "3. 스토어 본문 (Description)". I'm not Korean, I'm Dutch, so something also went wrong there.

Hope this helps you in your feedback and I wish you luck.

replies.author: hwantasticgames
replies.body:
Thank you so much for pointing that out! I hadn't realized that "3. 스토어 본문 (설명)" was left in there by mistake, so I really appreciate you catching it. The link is located right next to that text.

Also, thank you for the feedback regarding the copy sounding a bit too AI-generated. That was something I completely overlooked, and your perspective is super helpful. I'll make sure to polish it!

comments.author: hwantasticgames
comments.body:
Thank you all so much for the feedback. It's the middle of the night here in Korea, and reading through the comments literally made my face burn with embarrassment. The points about the UI caught me completely off guard, but as many of you pointed out, it's true—the artwork isn't particularly eye-catching.

When I first started developing this game, I thought that since it's a card game focused on cards on a table, the current visual quality wouldn't be a huge issue. Instead, I put most of my energy into designing deep stages and missions to make sure a simple card game could offer plenty of content and replayability.

Getting this kind of unfiltered feedback is fascinating, but honestly, it also stings quite a bit. Back when I worked at a game studio, my boss always teased me about having "zero aesthetic sense." It's a bit humbling (and kind of surreal) to see that flaw immediately exposed the moment I go solo, with so many people pointing out the exact same issue right away.

Looks like I have a lot of soul-searching and problem-solving ahead of me. To be honest, I actually liked the current UI, and since art is far from my strong suit, figuring out how to improve it feels a bit daunting. For now, though, I really need to get some sleep.

Thanks again, everyone. I truly appreciate all your honesty!

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
I have zero aesthetic sense too, and with my first game I learned the hard way that bad graphics can entirely ruin a game, no matter how good gameplay is. Nobody will give it a chance if they don't like what they see at first glance.  
And using AI art makes this even worse because of the negative bias, at the first thing they dislike they'll discard the whole project as AI slop.

It's a complex topic and I'm not qualified to give advice, but I can tell you there's plenty of paths to explore if you want to do good games no matter what.  
So please do your soul-searching and I'm sure you'll find your way.



Regarding this specific project, I think you have two options:

1) Release it as it is, even if chances of success are low. Nothing wrong with it, finishing and releasing anything at all is already a significant achievement. You can take the win, learn from the mistakes and release a better game next time. And since it's vibe coded I assume you didn't waste that much effort.

2) Redo all the graphics without AI. Either by yourself, or download a GUI pack from unity's asset store or [itch.io](http://itch.io) or wherever, download the cards too, etc. Then remove the AI disclosure from the steam page (you don't need to disclose AI coding, only things that are visible to the users).  
Even if it doesn't look much better, just by removing the AI stigma you are increasing your chances of success significantly (and no offense but you are not sacrificing much by replacing current graphics).

  
Hope that helps, congrats on the progress so far and stay strong my dude

replies.author: hwantasticgames
replies.body:
Great to meet a fellow zero aesthetic sense! Thanks so much for the support.  
Launching it as is would just be driving straight into failure. My goal is to participate in the upcoming Steam Next Fest, so I’m definitely going to put in the work to polish and improve it. Really appreciate your encouragement!

comments.author: PhotojournalistBig53
comments.body: All the comments complaining about 'it looks AI' in an ai gamedev sub is pretty horrifying tbh. Where are the mods on this one? This sub is supposed to be a safe space for AI gamedevs. If you don't like the way it looks, say what it is you don't like don't just tack on 'looks like AI slop' there are other subs for that.

replies.author: hwantasticgames
replies.body: Thank you for the kind comment! I’m genuinely not ashamed of making this game with AI—being able to bring an idea to life like this is such an exciting thing in itself. But at the end of the day, people like what they like, and if they don't, they don't. What I ultimately want is to make something people genuinely enjoy and want to buy, so I’m walking away from this with a lot of great takeaways and insights.
